name: Japanese New Year (Shōgatsu)
gift: Otoshidama money in small decorated envelopes (pochibukuro) for children; good-quality sweets or sake for hosts.
avoid: Sets of four; anything associated with funerals.

name: Lunar New Year
gift: Red envelopes with new bills, mandarin oranges in pairs, tea, premium snacks, liquor for elders, zodiac-themed keepsakes.
avoid: Clocks, scissors and knives, pears, white or black wrapping, amounts with the number 4.

name: Lantern Festival
gift: Lanterns, tangyuan (sweet rice balls) gift packs, riddle cards for families.
avoid: Ending the New Year season without thanking hosts who received you.

name: Holi
gift: Herbal colour (gulal) sets, sweets such as gujiya, thandai mixes, white kurtas for playing colours.

name: Eid al-Fitr
region: Muslim communities across South and Southeast Asia
gift: Dates and sweets hampers, Eidi (money) for children, fragrance (alcohol-free attar), prayer mats, modest clothing.
avoid: Alcohol, pork products, and anything not halal for food gifts. Dates depend on moon sighting.

name: White Day
gift: Return gifts for Valentine's chocolates: white chocolate, cookies, marshmallows, small accessories.
avoid: Forgetting colleagues who gave giri choco.

name: Songkran (Thai New Year)
gift: Jasmine-scented water and garlands for elders, fruit baskets, practical gifts for older relatives.
avoid: Gifts that need to stay dry if you are visiting during the water festival.

name: Children's Day (Kodomo no Hi)
gift: Koinobori carp streamers, kashiwa-mochi sweets, books and toys.
avoid: Nothing specific; keep gifts age appropriate.

name: Dragon Boat Festival (Duanwu)
gift: Zongzi (sticky rice dumplings) gift boxes, fragrant sachets, realgar-free herbal pouches.
avoid: Some families avoid saying 'happy' on this day; a simple 'Duanwu ankang' (wishing you good health) is a safe greeting.

name: Ochūgen (summer gift season)
gift: Chilled consumables: premium fruit, somen noodles, beer, coffee or tea sets, sent to bosses, clients and people you are indebted to.
avoid: Non-consumables, knives, stationery for superiors, sets of four.

name: Qixi Festival (Chinese Valentine's Day)
gift: Flowers, jewellery, chocolates, a handwritten card, matching keepsakes.
avoid: Pears (sound like 'parting'), umbrellas, shoes for a partner.

name: Raksha Bandhan
gift: Rakhi threads and sweets from sisters; brothers return gifts such as jewellery, gadgets, cosmetics or cash.
avoid: Leather gifts in strictly observant households.

name: Chuseok
gift: Premium gift sets: Korean beef (hanwoo), fruit (apples, pears), red ginseng, spam and oil sets, health supplements.
avoid: Shoes for a partner, handkerchiefs, writing names in red ink, sets of four.

name: Mid-Autumn Festival
region: China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Vietnam, Singapore, Malaysia
gift: Mooncake boxes, tea to pair with them, pomelos, lanterns for children.
avoid: Boxes of four mooncakes, clocks, white flower arrangements.

name: Diwali
region: India, Nepal, Singapore, Malaysia, Indian diaspora
gift: Sweets (mithai), dry-fruit boxes, diyas and candles, silver coins, home décor, gift hampers.
avoid: Leather and alcohol for traditional households; amounts ending in zero for cash gifts (add 1).

name: Oseibo (year-end gift season)
gift: Consumables for the New Year table: ham, seafood, sake, coffee and tea, premium seasonings.
avoid: Sending late without relabelling: after New Year, send it as Onenga (first week of January) or Kanchū mimai (mid-winter greeting).

name: Christmas
region: Philippines, South Korea, Japan, Singapore, worldwide
gift: In Japan: Christmas cake and couple gifts. In the Philippines: food baskets (noche buena) and family gifts. In Korea: couple gifts.
avoid: Applying Western norms blindly: in Japan Christmas Eve is a couples' occasion.
